hero_sub.text: Type a keyword in Safari's address bar, jump anywhere. Thirty built-in shortcuts, bang chaining, regex keywords, and optional URL rewriting — all editable, all on-device. A native Safari extension for macOS, iOS, and iPadOS.

hero_cta.text: Get it on the App Store

f1_d.text: g, d, b for search; w, mdn, ad for references; gh, so for code; y, spo, n for media; npm, cargo, pip, brew for package managers, and more.

f2_d.text: Change the trigger, URL template, default URL, or aliases. Add your own. Soft-delete with a 20-entry trash bin for recovery.

f3_d.text: Type !g foo !w bar to open Google in the current tab and Wikipedia in a new one. Configurable separator.

f4_d.text: Pattern-matched shortcuts like gh/(\S+)/(\S+) → github.com/$1/$2 for issue, PR, and repo navigation in one keystroke.

f5_d.text: Curated rules to redirect Twitter → Nitter, Reddit → old.reddit, YouTube → Piped, and other privacy-friendly frontends. All toggleable, all editable.

f6_d.text: As you type, friendly errors appear inline: missing URL protocol, invalid regex, capture-group mismatches, conflicting triggers.

f7_d.text: Built-in language picker with flag icons and native names. Defaults to your system locale; switch anytime from the top-right of the settings page.

f8_d.text: Built-in keywords compile to Safari's declarativeNetRequest rules — no visible flash before the redirect fires. The fastest possible path.

f9_d.text: No accounts, no cloud sync, no analytics. Your keyword list lives entirely on your device. Findbar collects zero data.

sec_how_title.text: Three steps to a faster address bar

s1_d.text: Download Findbar from the App Store. One purchase covers Mac, iPhone, and iPad via Family Sharing.

s2_d.text: Open Safari Settings → Extensions → enable Findbar. Grant the permissions it asks for.

s3_d.text: In Safari's address bar, type g followed by your search and press Enter. That's it. Edit and add keywords in the settings page anytime.

w1_d.text: Findbar uses Safari's native APIs (declarativeNetRequest, webNavigation, storage). Built ground-up for Safari, not a polyfill of Chrome's omnibox API which Safari doesn't have.

w2_d.text: No accounts. No telemetry. No cloud. Your keyword list, rewrite rules, and preferences live entirely on your device. Findbar never phones home.

w3_d.text: Translated into 32 non-English locales (Spanish, Japanese, Arabic, German, French, and many more) — switchable in-app, independent of your system language.

req.text: Requires macOS 14.0 (Sonoma) or later, or iOS / iPadOS 17.0 or later. Works with Safari 17+.

f_brand.text: Indie software studio. Building focused, privacy-first tools for Apple platforms.
